item.title: Ep 554: Macau’s separate legal framework lets Tesla deliver Grok to owners there while mainland China waits on licensing.
item.description: Tesla Shorts Time REAL-TIME TSLA price: $313.03 ▲ $1.65 (0.5%) Macau’s separate legal framework lets Tesla deliver Grok to owners there while mainland China waits on licensing. Top 12 News Items Tesla Grok Update in Macau, TSLAming (X) Tesla owners in Macau are already receiving the 2026.26 Summer Update that includes Grok integration. The rollout works because Macau operates under a separate legal and internet framework from Mainland China under “One Country, Two Systems,” so xAI avoids the special government licensing required elsewhere. This gives early access to the feature in a Chinese-speaking market without broader regulatory hurdles. The update arrives through the normal over-the-air channel and requires no additional hardware on supported vehicles. Observers note that the same code base remains unavailable on the mainland pending formal approvals. Source: x.com Tesla reports record vehicle deliveries amid profitability decline, EV Infrastructure News Tesla posted record vehicle deliveries while reporting a decline in profitability. The contrast highlights ongoing pressure on margins even as volume grows. Automotive gross margins narrowed despite higher unit counts, reflecting pricing adjustments and higher operating expenses. The company continues to allocate significant capital toward autonomy, robotics, and energy storage initiatives that have not yet offset the margin compression. Investors are watching whether the delivery momentum can stabilize cash flow in the coming quarters. Source: Google News Tesla Rolls Out 2026 Summer Update to Customer Vehicles With New Traction Control Options, autoevolution The update adds new traction control modes aimed at improving handling across different conditions. It reaches Model 3 and Model Y first, the vehicles that previously lacked dedicated drive modes for varied surfaces. The feature set includes selectable settings for snow, sand, and off-road use that adjust motor torque and stability systems in real time. Owners can access the modes through the existing drive-mode menu on the center screen. Rollout began with vehicles already on the 2026.26 software branch and will continue over the next several weeks. Source: Google News Tesla quietly closes mystery AI acquisition, still no details, Automotive World Tesla completed an undisclosed AI-related acquisition without releasing further information. The move adds to the company’s growing set of AI capabilities across vehicle and robotics programs. No purchase price, target company name, or integration timeline has been disclosed in regulatory filings or public statements. The transaction follows a pattern of smaller tuck-in deals aimed at strengthening internal machine-learning infrastructure. Analysts expect any material contribution to appear in future updates to Cortex or Dojo workloads. Source: Google News Musk says Tesla Semi self-driving is a year away, so truckers are safe, Electrek Elon Musk stated that unsupervised self-driving capability for the Tesla Semi remains about a year away. The timeline suggests current truck drivers face limited near-term displacement from the technology. Production of the supervised version continues at Giga Texas, with early fleet customers still evaluating range and payload economics on real routes. Musk’s comment came during a public appearance and aligns with the company’s broader caution on regulatory approval for unsupervised operation. Fleets are therefore planning diesel-replacement decisions around 2027 or later. Source: Google News Tesla's Optimus Faces Investor Doubts Over Near-Term Profitability; Musk Fires Back, Calling Rivals' Demos "All an Act", finance.biggo.com Investors questioned whether Optimus can generate meaningful revenue soon, prompting Elon Musk to dismiss competing humanoid demos as staged. The exchange underscores the gap between current development status and commercial expectations. Musk emphasized that Tesla’s internal testing focuses on useful tasks rather than choreographed displays. This follows yesterday’s discussion on Optimus production targets and keeps attention on when visible factory output will begin. The debate centers on whether early units will first serve Tesla’s own factories or external buyers. Source: Google News Hong Kong-listed robotics-related stocks rose as Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot approaches mass production by year-end, accelerating the industrialization of humanoid robots., 富途牛牛 Shares of Hong Kong robotics companies climbed on expectations that Optimus will reach mass production before the end of the year. The movement reflects broader market interest in the humanoid robotics supply chain. Component suppliers tied to actuators, sensors, and battery packs saw the largest gains during the session. The optimism stems from Tesla’s repeated statements that low-volume builds will begin in late 2026 ahead of higher-rate output in 2027. Investors are tracking any updates on supplier contracts or tooling orders that could confirm the schedule. Source: Google News A UK owner was eyeing Powerwall 3, then Tesla disabled one battery and ordered a recall swap, The Cool Down A UK customer preparing to install a Powerwall 3 had one battery unit disabled by Tesla, which then initiated a recall replacement. The incident illustrates quality-control steps that can interrupt customer deployment timelines. Tesla remotely limited the unit’s operation after detecting an anomaly during pre-installation checks. The owner was notified through the Tesla app and scheduled for a swap at no cost. Such interventions protect long-term reliability but can delay expected energy-cost savings for new buyers. Source: Google News Homeowner buys Powerwall to dodge California peak rates under NEM 3.0, then watched it pull from the grid, The Cool Down A California homeowner installed a Powerwall specifically to avoid peak-rate charges under NEM 3.0 rules, only to observe the unit drawing power from the grid. The outcome points to configuration or software behavior that can undermine intended bill-saving use cases. The system was expected to discharge during expensive evening hours and recharge from solar during the day. Instead, telemetry showed grid imports during periods when solar production should have covered household load. Tesla support is investigating whether firmware settings or inverter logic require adjustment for NEM 3.0 compliance. Source: Google News Something Doesn’t Add Up About The Rivian R2’s EPA Efficiency Rating, InsideEVs The Rivian R2 carries the same official EPA efficiency rating as the Tesla Model Y, yet real-world testing showed the R2 consuming more energy. The discrepancy highlights differences between lab ratings and on-road performance for the two vehicles. Independent tests recorded the R2 using 18 to 26 percent more electricity per mile than the Model Y under comparable conditions. The gap appears most pronounced on highways and during cold-weather drives. Rivian has not yet commented on the test methodology or potential software updates to close the difference. The appearance provided another public forum for Tesla-related topics outside traditional earnings calls. Tesla’s automotive and energy revenue combined now represent a meaningful fraction of Ford’s total despite fewer legacy product lines. Both companies face margin pressure from EV transition costs, yet Tesla’s growth rate remains higher on a percentage basis. Here are the most interesting, fresh Tesla developments that have everyone talking. FSD v14.3.6 parks perfectly at Sheetz despite other issues - An owner reported the software navigated a busy Sheetz lot, handled cars at gas pumps, and completed both outbound and home parking without issues. The experience stood out for parking-lot performance compared with prior releases. Multiple stops during the same drive showed consistent low-speed maneuvering around moving vehicles and tight spaces. The driver noted that earlier versions had required more intervention in similar retail environments. These reports add to a growing set of owner videos documenting incremental improvements in the v14 series. Source: x.com FSD handles crowded Target parking lot successfully - The same owner noted the system found spots in a packed Target lot and repeated the result at another shopping center the same morning. These cases add to real-world data on unsupervised parking maneuvers. The software identified open spaces, executed precise reverse maneuvers, and avoided pedestrians without driver input. The consistency across two different locations in one day suggests the latest release handles variable lighting and dynamic obstacles more reliably. Owners continue to share similar clips as the update propagates. Source: x.com No parking issues with Tesla FSD v14.3.6 so far - A follow-up post confirmed zero parking problems encountered across multiple stops. The consistency suggests incremental gains in low-speed navigation logic. The owner tested the system at several retail destinations with varying lot layouts and traffic density. No phantom stops or incorrect path planning occurred during these maneuvers. Continued real-world use will determine whether the pattern holds across more diverse conditions. Source: x.com Analyzing Tesla In Comparison To Competitors In Automobiles Industry - The review places Tesla’s metrics against other automakers on revenue, margins, and growth rates. It supplies a side-by-side view of where Tesla stands relative to traditional players. Key comparisons include operating margins, cash-flow generation, and capital-expenditure intensity across legacy and EV-focused manufacturers. The analysis highlights Tesla’s higher research-and-development spend as a percentage of revenue compared with most peers. Readers can use the data to assess how scale and vertical integration affect profitability trajectories. Source: Google News Tesla (TSLA) Stock Still Looks Fully Priced As Services Revenue Jumps 50% - Services revenue rose 50 percent, yet the analysis concludes the stock valuation remains elevated relative to that growth. The piece weighs the services contribution against overall share pricing. Growth in the segment stems from increased Supercharger utilization, insurance uptake, and connectivity subscriptions. Even with the jump, the valuation multiple applied to the services line exceeds those of comparable software or aftermarket businesses. The report suggests investors are still pricing in substantial future contributions from autonomy and robotics that have not yet materialized. Source: Google News Short Spot Tesla achieved record deliveries while profitability fell. The gap shows that higher volume alone has not offset rising costs or pricing pressure. The company continues to invest heavily in AI, robotics, and autonomy programs that have yet to generate offsetting revenue. Margin compression appears across both automotive and energy segments, leaving less cash for the very initiatives driving the spending. Management has signaled that near-term results will remain volatile until new product lines reach meaningful scale. Source: Google News Tesla First Principles Regional regulatory differences can accelerate or block software feature rollouts even when the underlying hardware and code are identical. Tesla’s Grok integration reached Macau owners first because the territory’s separate legal and internet rules bypassed the licensing process required on the mainland. That single distinction turns a uniform product into a staggered release schedule across one country. The same code base that works immediately in Macau must still clear additional approvals before it reaches the much larger mainland market. This creates an uneven customer experience and forces Tesla to maintain parallel support documentation for different regulatory environments. The same pattern appears in energy products where local rate structures and interconnection rules shape real-world performance. A California homeowner installed a Powerwall to avoid peak charges under NEM 3.0, yet the unit drew from the grid instead. In the UK, a planned Powerwall 3 install was halted when Tesla remotely disabled a battery and triggered a recall swap. These cases show that grid-interactive software must satisfy both technical and regulatory constraints that vary sharply by jurisdiction. Configuration files and firmware branches therefore multiply, raising the cost of testing and customer-service staffing. For Tesla the result is a fragmented deployment map: features and hardware reach customers at different speeds depending on local rules rather than engineering readiness alone. That fragmentation raises the cost of support, testing, and customer communication while slowing the revenue recognition tied to each new capability. Over time the company’s ability to standardize across borders will depend less on code quality and more on how quickly regulators converge on common standards for AI assistants and grid storage. The business-model implication is clear: every month of regulatory delay directly reduces the present value of the services and energy revenue streams that investors already price into the stock.
